This feat is probably one of Akagi’s most methodical feats unlike his other strategies which involves more of a series of tactics that don’t interlock with each other as well, but in this Arc Akagi had a clear strategic core throughout which makes his a valuable feat for scaling Akagi.
I already made an explanation of specific rules of mahjong significant in Akagi in my Ichikawa strategy doc so you can go read the rules of mahjong section on that doc:

Chonbo, it is the penalty point you pay if you break a rule. The only rule that is broken in this game is the rule of “you can’t call Riichi unless you are in Tenpai”. If you do a Chonbo and you are caught for it you must pay a total of 8000 points.

Also a common way mahjong players read each other's hands is though seeing a tile discard comes from “inside their hand” or “Tsumo-Giri”. When people are playing mahjong they check if the opponents discarded tile came from inside their 13 tile hand meaning it was a part of their hand but now it's not, or was an unneeded tile they had before. If its a Tsumo-Giri it means the tile they just pulled was not needed to progress their hand,

I will just introduce the Yaku that are significant in this game so you can better understand Akagi’s strategies. I sometimes translate the Yaku’s name from the top of my head and not check the official translations so the way I refer to some Yaku might be different. Even if you are familiar with mahjong if some ways I refer to Yaku confuse you please refer to this section,

It is a Yakuman hand or in other words the highest Yaku a hand can have, a Yakuman can be achieved if your hand has more than 13 Han (Han is just the total number of Yaku your hand has + the number of Dora) or you form specific patterns that is given Yakuman value. For this case it requires you to form 4 triplets (3 of the same kind) without calling any one of them, also you must win with either a Tsumo, or a Ron for the head part, if your Ron tile is what completes a triplet this Yaku does not count.

Once you declare Riichi you have the option to open your hand, meaning your hand which is normally hidden to everyone is opened and revealed, this means everyone will know what you are waiting on and what your Yaku is. It adds 1 Yaku in addition to the 1 Yaku a Riichi adds to your hand. Because Riichi is a Yaku where you can’t call, of-course you can’t do any calls to earn this Yaku either.
If you do a Ron from the last tile that is discarded for the round it adds one Yaku to your hand, it can be done no matter how many tiles you called in the game.
A Yaku that can be formed no matter how much you call, if your hand does not contain any 1,9 or word tiles it grants you one Yaku.
If your hand has three triplets of the same number in all 3 suits, so if you had a triplet of 6 souzu, a triplet of 6 manzu and a triplet of 6 pinzu you would have this Yaku.

This is fiction we are talking about so as a part of Akagi’s world building, sensing and exploiting the flow of the game is a valid strategic move. : A follow up to reason 3 but it allowed Akagi to further confuse Urabe by showing that Akagi is irrational since he will not rest on a cheaper hand no matter what, making Urabe further unsure of what kind of person.
